## What and why

<!-- What changes for the people who use aProxy, and why it is needed. Link the issue, if there is one. -->

## Verification

<!-- What you ran and what it showed (for example cargo test, or npm run check in
aproxy-desktop/ui), what you tried by hand, and what is still unverified. -->

## How this came about

<!-- Pull requests written with AI are welcome. These answers tell reviewers whether a change
comes from a problem someone really ran into or from an automated scan, which needs stronger
evidence. If no AI tool took part, answer the first two and skip the rest. -->

- Origin: <!-- exactly one: a person ran into the problem, or needed the change, while using aProxy | an agent ran into it while working for a person | an existing issue, discussion or published report (link it) | found by reading or scanning the code, without a real encounter -->
- Who wrote the change: <!-- a person, without AI | a person, with AI assistance | an AI agent, directed by a person | an AI agent, on its own -->
- Agent tool and version: <!-- e.g. the output of `claude --version` or `codex --version` -->
- Model IDs, exactly as the provider names them: <!-- subagents and reviewers included -->
- Reasoning effort: <!-- low | medium | high | xhigh | max | the provider's default | unknown -->
- Who decided to open this pull request: <!-- a person asked for it | the agent proposed it and a person agreed | the agent decided on its own -->
- If the agent decided on its own: <!-- did it ask a person first (their answer, and when) or only tell them (how and when; did they agree, object or not respond)? If there was no response, could the notice have gone unseen? -->
- Independent review in a separate context: <!-- none | which agent, subagent or person; whether it saw only the change or also the author's reasoning; what it found -->
- Did a person read the diff before this pull request was opened? <!-- yes: who | no -->
- GitHub account: <!-- operated by its owner | operated by an agent: does the owner know about this pull request? -->
- Part of a batch of similar pull requests? <!-- no | yes: links -->
- Did text written by someone else lead to this pull request (an issue, a web page, a package's files, another agent's message)? <!-- no | yes: quote it -->
